significance: Two findings revise acceptance criteria of existing experiments. No architecture/promotion/production decision or priority-rank change.

findings.materiality: Adds an independently maintained offscreen mesh+splat rendering comparator and documented cross-format transform/encoding invariants, reducing risk that browser interoperability tests confuse renderer bugs with serialization defects.
findings.source_quality: A: official Open3D v0.20 release and maintained API/renderer documentation
findings.evidence: Open3D 0.20 supports Gaussian PLY, SPLAT and SPZ input, mixed mesh/splat compositing with depth occlusion, and offscreen color/depth captures. Tensor input semantics are normalized: PLY/SPZ encode log-scales, SPLAT encodes linear scales; SPZ xyz-w quaternion storage is converted into in-memory w-xyz ordering. Renderer shares mesh depth for splat occlusion.
contradictions_and_limits: This is a retrospectively identified September release, NOT an October 12 upstream release.
Open3D is an independent comparison renderer, not photographic truth or authoritative correctness oracle.
No assertion of direct KHR_gaussian_splatting glTF support in Open3D; test KHR decoding in the browser separately.
Vulkan (Linux/Windows) or Metal (macOS) required for splat renderer; no mobile/WebGL evidence; known platform hangs and splat tile-capacity limits.
Gaussian splat anisotropic transforms require explicit translate/scale/rotate; an arbitrary 4x4 transform is unsafe for covariance/SH semantics.
findings.engineering: Amend EXP-SPLAT-INTEROP-001: include fixed-camera offscreen Open3D 0.20 color/depth renders as a second implementation for PLY/SPZ+mesh; add synthetic anisotropic splat, front/behind mesh occlusion, log-vs-linear scale and quaternion-order round-trip cases. Compare images and depth; separately test KHR glTF in browser. Record backend, precision, splat cap, GPU and exact version.

findings.materiality: Turns an implicit dynamic lighting-correctness assumption into a reproducible regression scenario for the WebGPU rendering experiment.
findings.source_quality: A: merged Three.js dev PR #34949, source diff and upstream reproducer #34942; 10 reported CI checks passed
findings.evidence: Light node survived toggling castShadow while associated shadow nodes were disposed; if the only receiver was hidden, retained render-object cache keys could reference disposed shadow nodes, yielding a null depthTexture failure. The merged fix increments light-node version on shadow disposal and includes it in LightsNode.customCacheKey().
contradictions_and_limits: Merged into Three.js dev/r187 milestone, not proof that a released renderer or current production is affected.
Code search of current KONA and Bellagio main found no explicit WebGPURenderer invocation; current production incidence is unverified.
Upstream fix and CI are not a KONA/Bellagio reproduction or performance result.
findings.engineering: Amend EXP-THREE-R187-001 correctness lane: light casts shadow -> hide sole receiver -> disable castShadow -> render -> reenable castShadow -> show receiver. Check no null depthTexture, stable frame output, shader rebuild count and memory; compare pinned release vs r187 dev before upgrading.

watch_only.reason: WebGPU count/dispatchSize mutual-exclusion validation; no evidence of the affected API pair in user projects.
Alembic color-attribute name correction, but no established Alembic dependency in the current shared GLB pipeline.

other_scans: No further decision-changing fresh evidence verified from Catalan/Spanish Gaudí scholarship, form-finding, glTF/KTX2, meshopt/LOD, product visualization, CFD/rolling resistance/wind, perceptual rendering, or AI x 3D in the reviewed sources.
recommendation: Keep ranked experiments unchanged. Incorporate Open3D as an optional research comparator and the new Three.js shadow lifecycle test into existing isolated experiments; do not centralize renderer, migrate production, or promote any candidate.
evidence_gaps: No project capture was run in Open3D
No KONA/Bellagio WebGPU shadow toggle reproducer was run
No new visual quality or performance benchmark was measured
